# A timed-out stack return carries the coordinator's claim-pass record

## Context

The first CI red carrying #19812's proof: Emmy's grid-only PR #19804 at `d7c1a645c6`, run [38914922511](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38914922511) job [117019879144](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38914922511/job/117019879144), 2026-10-16 14:23Z — scene 5's second take, both attempts (tests 13 and 14 of the `e2e-brain (10/10)` shard), the shape #19810 recorded on three heads. The toolbar diff touches no Workstation file; Emmy's triage DM (14:28Z) keeps the toolbar goal and leaves the causal fix here.

What the proof says, both attempts identical up to window ids:

- `participation`: `affordances true`, target `neo-crosswindow-drag-target-2` in main — main's target exists, the second instance of this page life.
- `coordinator`: `activeTargetZoneId null`; the pointer arbiter live, token `gesture-4`, `claimCount 0`, no winner; `nativeArbiterWindowIds` holds the source vessel's window only; `nativeHoverWindowIds []`.
- `sourceZone`: `neo-dock-tab-sortzone-13`, `dockGroupNodeId workstation-vessel-tabs:metrics`, `stackDragActive true`, `dragProxy true` — the source drag armed.
- `windows`: main `innerRect {x 10, y 10, 1280×800}`; source `{x 1383, y 938, 320×240}`.
- `owners`: `owned [metrics → tearout-metrics]`, `connections []`, `pendingRetirements []`.

Against #19810's three hypotheses: main's participation and target are present (not "never re-armed"); the registry reads as a committed vessel's normal state (owned, connection consumed) — but a record retained from the first take would read the same, because `owned[]` omits the record's `windowId`; main's `innerRect` is sane, and the node and rect the cursor aimed at never reached the log: the driver's proof carries `aimed` (#19812) while scene 5's assertion message prints a fixed field list without it.

## The Problem

The pointer path resolves its claim in `DragCoordinator#resolveClaimedTarget`, and every pass records its own decision on the coordinator's ring: `recordClaimResolution` pushes `{outcome: 'group-absent' | 'claimed' | 'no-claim', candidates: [{windowId, skipped: 'source-or-excluded' | 'ownership' | 'no-stable-identity' | 'no-accepts-handler'} | {windowId, stableTargetId, innerResolved, intersects, accepts}], sourceOwnershipId, groupSize, retiredStableIds, gestureToken}` into `claimTrace` (limit 40), the token stamped at decision time. That record is the one surface that separates the causes the snapshot leaves standing — main's zone absent from the group, refused by ownership admission, outside its `innerRect`, or refusing the window-local hit-test — and it is the one surface the unready proof does not carry. It is exposed through the coordinator's `toJSON()` for the Neural Link's drag-state route, which CI never calls.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs:129` attaches `claimSurfaces` to an unready read; `describeClaimSurfaces` (:151–192) already holds the live arbiter (`pointerClaimArbiter`, or `nativeClaimArbiters.get(nativeWindowId)`); `owned` at :188 maps `{itemId, windowName}` only.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:823–937` `resolveClaimedTarget`; `:959` `recordClaimResolution(entry, gestureToken)` — its JSDoc: the ring spans gestures, so a reader filters by the entry's own token, never the token live at serialization; `:170` `claimTrace`, `:179` `claimTraceLimit`.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:3165–3173` — scene 5's return assertion message (`sourceArm`, `closeReceipt`, `phaseOrder`, `remoteSnapshot`, `sourceItemIds`, `sourceWindowGone`, `transfer`).
- `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs:814` — `proof.aimed` (#19812).
- `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs:359–420` — the unready/ready `claimSurfaces` case.
- Design authority: not applicable — diagnostics only; no behaviour is called wrong.

## The Fix

Instrumentation, no behaviour change, one PR:

1. `describeClaimSurfaces` adds `claimTrace`: the coordinator's entries whose `gestureToken` equals the live arbiter's `token`, newest last, at most the last 3, deep-cloned (plain ids, strings and booleans — the entries hold no zone references). `null` when there is no coordinator or no live arbiter.
2. `owners.owned[]` entries carry `windowId: entry?.windowId ?? null`, so a record retained from an earlier take (a window that no longer exists) is distinguishable from the current vessel's.
3. Scene 5's assertion message adds `aimed: returnResult.proof?.aimed`.
4. The unit case at :359 extends: a coordinator whose `claimTrace` holds entries of two tokens → only the live token's ride, bounded to 3, newest last; `owned[].windowId`; a ready read still carries no `claimSurfaces`.

## Follow-up

The fix, filed from the first red that carries this record: the named conjunct, its run id, the repair.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unready pointer read's `claimSurfaces.claimTrace` carries only the live gesture's claim-pass records (token match), at most 3, newest last, each candidate with its reason; `claimSurfaces.owners.owned[].windowId` is present; a ready read is unchanged — one unit case.
- [ ] Scene 5's failure message prints `aimed` beside `remoteSnapshot`.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next red of the shard names the refusing conjunct from the log alone, by run id.

## Out of Scope

The behaviour fix; rerunning past reds; scenes 2 and 4; the hosted-CI lane (#19655); changing `claimTraceLimit`; a Neural Link call from the spec on failure (CI runs the spec, not the tools).

## Avoided Traps

- Fixing from the snapshot: four causes survive it; the resolver's own record is cheaper than a fifth hypothesis — #18215's lesson, the poll that could not see the state it waited for.
- Printing the whole ring: forty entries across gestures bury the live one; the token filter and the bound keep the proof readable.
- Reading the token live at serialization — the entry's stamped token is the attribution (`recordClaimResolution` JSDoc).
